 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Atlanta United faces a grim reality as the MLS regular season winds down. The club sits in 12th place within the Eastern Conference with a record of 9-18-6. Their defense has allowed 57 goals while scoring only 43, resulting in a negative 14 goal differential. This gap is far too wide to overcome in a single weekend. The team needs to stop giving up points if they want any chance of making the postseason.
 New York Red Bulls enter this matchup with a much better standing at ninth place. They have won 11 games this season and hold a clear edge in the standings. Per FOX Sports , the Red Bulls are 9-11-5 when playing against other Eastern Conference teams. Atlanta has struggled in conference play with a record of 6-13-6. The difference in performance between these two clubs is stark and undeniable.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Defensive Woes Define The Season
 The numbers tell a brutal story about Atlanta's inability to protect their goal. The team has surrendered 5.1 goals per game over their last 10 matches. This defensive collapse has cost them dearly in the standings. Even with Miguel Almiron contributing seven goals and seven assists, the team cannot win when the back line fails. Breel Embolo has added three goals and one assist in the last 10 games, but offense alone cannot fix a broken defense.
 In contrast, the Red Bulls have shown they can score freely but also struggle to hold leads. Their last 10 games saw them allow 4.8 goals per game. Yet they managed to average 3.9 goals while taking 15.0 shots on goal per match. Julian Hall has found the net four times in his last 10 games. The Red Bulls also benefit from a strong home record, having won 29 of 45 games where they scored two or more goals. Atlanta must find a way to stop scoring their own team out of the game.
 Injuries Complicate The Final Push
 The roster depth for Atlanta is thin as the pressure mounts. Daniel Chica is listed as not expected to play due to injury. The Red Bulls face similar issues with Cameron Harper and Justin Che both sidelined. These absences remove key bodies from the field just when the team needs them most. Every player must step up because there is no bench strength to rely on in this tight race.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Atlanta cannot afford to lose this match if they want to keep their hopes alive. The team is currently 15-8-7 in their last 10 games overall, but the conference record tells a different story. They need to turn around their performance against league rivals immediately. The gap between ninth and 12th place is more than a number; it reflects a season of missed opportunities.
 The final test for both clubs arrives on Saturday at 4 p.m. EST in Harrison, New Jersey.
